event_risk.note: Deterministic event-risk layer (docs/EVENT_AWARENESS.md §3, §8): phases, relevance, dominance, per-asset event risk, EVENT RISK MODE and the pre-event overlay. Scores are 0-100 configured weightings, never probabilities. A component that cannot be computed is left out and the weights are renormalised over the measured ones (listed in 'missing'). The overlay never changes a published decision: it adds event_risk, adjusted_confidence and trade_status beside it. 1.1.0: session windows for date-only rows, regime sensitivity independent of unexposed drivers, exposure floor for per-asset risk, capped relevance for unmapped events, importance-gated risk mode (also for live VERY HIGH central-bank decisions), fact-backed AI surprise classification only. 1.1.1: a date-only row without a session or class window is labelled 'whole day, <zone> time' (default_label, zone_names), never an internal term. 1.2.0 (event-risk audit 2 Oct): EVENT RISK MODE also for a verified unscheduled event of class importance >= importance_min first seen within risk_mode.active_minutes (EVR-3); a date-only central-bank decision follows its ingested official statement (EVR-5); release_documents and the snapshot's released_today keep a released key event visible with what was published (EVR-4); a publication stamp without a clock time no longer starts an unscheduled event's active window (unscheduled.date_only_zones, EVR-6). 1.3.0: the outcome of a scheduled release is read from the stored official series and attached to its calendar row (release_documents.classes[].series, period_rule, attach_window_hours; backend/releases.py), the EventObject carries `outcome`, and released_today states the outcome text with the measured reaction (EVR-4).

date_only_sessions.note: A date-only row (time_known false) is APPROACHING ('time TBA') until the end of its release window, then POST_EVENT for the class post_event_minutes, then RESOLVED; it never becomes IMMINENT, RELEASED, IN_PROGRESS or EVENT RISK MODE. The window is the class window, else the session of the row ('session' field, else a time_basis pattern), else the publisher's local day (provider_routing.calendars.country_timezones). 'end' 24:00 is the end of that day. After-close earnings are published between the 16:00 ET close and the end of the extended session (20:00 ET). The publisher's-day window is labelled default_label with the zone's name from zone_names (else the zone's city).

relevance.regime_sensitivity_note: Static mean of the event's exposure over every regime driver (an event property), raised toward 100 by moving_exposed_boost x the exposure share of the drivers that move AND are exposed. A moving driver the event is not exposed to never lowers it.

unmapped.note: An event exposing no tracked asset (class OTHER or no exposure mapping) cannot outrank mapped events: relevance and dominance are capped (below next_event_min_relevance).

asset_risk.note: Per-asset event risk of an exposed asset = relevance x (exposure_floor + (1 - exposure_floor) x exposure weight): an exposed asset carries at least exposure_floor of the event's relevance; an unexposed asset carries none.

risk_mode.note: EVENT RISK MODE: a timed event within 'minutes' (or RELEASED / IN_PROGRESS) that is CRITICAL or whose class importance is at least importance_min; a RELEASED / IN_PROGRESS decision of live_classes at one of live_levels; a verified UNRESOLVED unscheduled event that is CRITICAL, or whose class importance is at least importance_min while it exposes tracked assets and was first seen at most active_minutes ago. Date-only rows never qualify.
risk_mode.active_minutes_note: EVR-3: how long after the app first saw a verified unscheduled event of class importance >= importance_min (GEO_ENERGY, CB_STATEMENT_UNSCHEDULED: 90) EVENT RISK MODE stays on for it. The composite relevance of an unscheduled class could not reach CRITICAL (maximum 89.0 with the default pricing uncertainty), so the mode never switched on for a verified Hormuz closure; the importance gate scheduled events already use now applies, bounded in time (4 h: the first reaction and its follow-through; the event stays ACTIVE EVENT RISK for active_window_hours).

adjustment.base_confidence_basis: |decision score| (conviction, not a probability) x (1 - pre-event penalty)

surprise.note: event.surprise {assessment, source, evidence_ids, validated} (docs/EVENT_AWARENESS.md §8). Post-event grading, scenario resolution and trade status use only a stored interpretation with source 'ai' whose next_events item for the event cites at least one evidence id of an official document of that event (official_documents below) ingested before the interpretation was generated, made after the release and, while a priced headline waited for guidance, after the guidance ended. The latest such assessment per event is used (a later fallback or a run without the event never removes it). Anything else is UNDETERMINED and never grades.

official_documents.note: CONFIRMED news events whose direct, official evidence comes from the bank's own source and was published from match_before_minutes before the event time to match_after_hours after it. The kind comes from the document title (first matching kind, in this order).

unscheduled.date_only_zones_note: EVR-6: a publication stamp at exact midnight in one of these publisher zones is a date without a clock time (an OFAC notice dated '2 Oct' is stored as 00:00 New York). It is not a publication time: the event's active window and decay then start when the app first saw it, and first_seen_utc is always the app's own first-seen time (published_utc carries the stamp, published_date_only says it has no clock time).

release_documents.note: EVR-4: the official document that published a scheduled release, the outcome read from the stored official series, and the snapshot's released_today list. A CONFIRMED news event whose direct, official evidence comes from one of the class sources, published from match_before_minutes before the scheduled time (a date-only row: its release window) to match_after_hours after it, and whose title or summary contains one of the phrases, is the release document of that class (central-bank classes use surprise.official_documents sources and kinds). released_today lists the scheduled events of the current Europe/Bucharest day that were released, of class importance >= min_importance and exposing tracked assets, for which something published is held: the outcome text from the official series ('series' below), else that document's summary, else the calendar row's actual. They stay listed after the event resolves, so the day's key release (NFP) does not vanish from the opening screen, with the measured reaction appended once it exists. match_before_minutes is wide because publishers stamp the feed item before the embargo time (the BLS employment item is stamped 07:51 ET for the 08:30 ET release).
release_documents.outcome_note: Outcome (backend/releases.py): 'series' per class lists the stored official series (official_series rows '<provider>:<series>:<period>', 'fallback' a second id with the same numbers, e.g. FRED's copy of a BLS series) that publish the release's headline numbers and how each is shown: 'change' (value minus the previous period's value: payrolls in thousands -> '+29k'), 'level' (the value: unemployment '4.2%'), 'pct_change' (percent change on the previous period: CPI m/m) or 'yoy' (percent change on the period `periods` earlier, 12 for a monthly index). The text names each metric with its previous reading ('payrolls +29k (prev +133k), unemployment 4.2% (prev 4.1%)'); the series marked 'headline' gives the calendar row its actual and previous. An outcome attaches only when the newest stored period of a series is the release's reference period: the row's own reference_period, else the class period_rule ('previous_month': the month before the scheduled day in series_zone; 'previous_week': the week ending the last Friday at least three days before it). It is attached to the calendar row (actual, previous, unit, metrics, values_source = the series provider, actual_ingested_at = when the app first stored that period, never later) from attach_before_minutes before the scheduled time to attach_window_hours after it, stored in macro_releases, alerted (MACRO_RELEASE) and observed (the MACRO_RELEASE refresh trigger). Consensus is never invented: a release with an outcome and no consensus records no surprise. The release watch polls the series providers right after a mapped release (official_data.release_poll).
